title: Deciding with advice within a time bound
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $\alpha$ and $T$ assign a Boolean list and a natural number, respectively, to each input length. The machine decides $L$ with advice $\alpha$ within time $T$ if, for every Boolean word $x$, on the encoded pair consisting of $x$ and $\alpha(|x|)$ it computes within $T(|x|)$ steps the one-symbol output indicating whether $x$ belongs to $L$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
Advice function assigning a Boolean list to each natural input length
Time-bound function assigning a natural number to each natural input length
The stated computation condition holds for every Boolean input word
